title: Dress & Ornament at Ráth Glas
summary: What the small finds from the ringfort tell us about how its inhabitants dressed, fastened their cloaks, and carried their belongings in the early medieval period.

blocks.heading: Fastening the cloak
blocks.text: The woollen cloak (brat) was the outer garment of early medieval Ireland, and it was fastened at the shoulder with a pin. The ringed pin from the occupation layer in Trench 1 is the classic everyday fastener of the 10th and 11th centuries: cheap to cast, easy to lose, and found in their hundreds from Dublin to Iceland.

blocks.heading: Personal adornment
blocks.text: Smaller items of adornment travelled far along the same routes as the people who wore them. The cobalt-blue glass bead from the souterrain fill and the tinned strap-end with its interlace ornament both speak to a household with access to fine goods, whether by trade, gift, or patronage.

blocks.heading: Grooming
blocks.text: Composite combs are among the most personal objects to survive from the period. The decorated comb fragment from Trench 1 was used long enough for its teeth to wear before it was discarded — a small, intimate trace of daily life inside the ringfort.
